MASTER SOFTWARE SERVICES AND TECHNOLOGY AGREEMENT

Effective Date: January 1, 2026

This Master Software Services and Technology Agreement ("Agreement") is
entered into between Alpha Technologies Ltd. ("Company") and Beta Solutions
Inc. ("Provider"). The parties agree to the following terms and conditions.

1. SERVICES

Provider shall provide software development, maintenance, technical support,
data processing, cloud infrastructure management, and related technology
services requested by Company from time to time. Provider shall perform the
services in a professional and commercially reasonable manner and shall use
qualified personnel to perform its obligations under this Agreement.

Provider shall maintain appropriate technical and organizational measures to
protect Company systems and information and shall notify Company without
undue delay of any material security incident affecting the services.

2. PAYMENT TERMS

Company shall pay Provider the fees specified in each applicable Statement of
Work. Unless otherwise stated in a Statement of Work, invoices shall be
submitted monthly and shall be payable within thirty (30) days after receipt.

If Company disputes an invoice in good faith, Company shall notify Provider
within ten (10) business days after receipt of the invoice and shall identify
the disputed amount and the reason for the dispute. The undisputed portion
shall remain payable according to the original payment schedule.

Provider may charge interest on undisputed overdue amounts at the lesser of
one percent (1%) per month or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law.
Provider shall not suspend critical services solely because of a disputed
invoice while the dispute is being resolved in good faith.

3. CONFIDENTIALITY

Each party may receive confidential business, technical, financial, security,
customer, product, or other proprietary information belonging to the other
party. The receiving party shall use such confidential information solely for
the purpose of performing or receiving services under this Agreement.

The receiving party shall not disclose confidential information to any third
party except to its employees, contractors, professional advisers, or
subprocessors who have a legitimate need to know such information and who
are bound by confidentiality obligations no less protective than those in
this Agreement.

The confidentiality obligations in this section shall not apply to information
that the receiving party can demonstrate was publicly available without
breach of this Agreement, was already lawfully known to the receiving party,
was independently developed without use of confidential information, or was
lawfully received from a third party without confidentiality restrictions.

Upon termination of this Agreement, each party shall, upon written request,
return or securely destroy the other party's confidential information, except
for copies required to be retained by law or maintained automatically in
ordinary-course backup systems.

4. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND IP ASSIGNMENT

All intellectual property rights in software, documentation, designs,
reports, specifications, and other deliverables specifically created by
Provider for Company under a Statement of Work shall be owned by Company
upon payment of the applicable fees, except for Provider's pre-existing
materials, tools, libraries, frameworks, and general know-how.

To the extent any intellectual property rights in a deliverable do not
automatically vest in Company, Provider hereby assigns to Company all right,
title, and interest in such intellectual property rights, including applicable
copyrights, patent rights, and other proprietary rights.

Provider retains ownership of its pre-existing technology and development
tools. Provider grants Company a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive,
royalty-free license to use any Provider pre-existing materials incorporated
into a deliverable to the extent necessary for Company to use, maintain, and
modify that deliverable.

5. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

Except for liability arising from a party's fraud, willful misconduct,
violation of confidentiality obligations, infringement or misappropriation of
intellectual property rights, or indemnification obligations under this
Agreement, neither party shall be liable to the other party for any indirect,
incidental, special, consequential, exemplary, or punitive damages, including
loss of profits, revenues, business opportunities, or anticipated savings,
whether arising in contract, tort, or otherwise.

Subject to the exclusions stated above, each party's aggregate liability
arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the total fees
paid or payable by Company to Provider under the applicable Statement of Work
during the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.

The limitations in this section shall apply to the maximum extent permitted
by applicable law.

6. INDEMNIFICATION

Provider shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Company, its affiliates,
and their respective officers, directors, employees, and agents from and
against any third-party claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and
reasonable attorneys' fees arising from or relating to any allegation that
the services or deliverables provided by Provider infringe or
misappropriate a third party's intellectual property rights.

Provider shall also indemnify Company against third-party claims arising from
Provider's gross negligence, willful misconduct, or violation of applicable
data protection or information security laws in connection with the services.

Company shall promptly notify Provider of any indemnified claim and shall
provide reasonable cooperation in the defense of such claim. Provider shall
not settle any claim in a manner that admits fault by Company or imposes
non-monetary obligations on Company without Company's prior written consent.

7. TERMINATION

Either party may terminate this Agreement for material breach by the other
party if the breach remains uncured for thirty (30) days after written
notice describing the breach in reasonable detail.

Company may terminate a Statement of Work for convenience upon thirty (30)
days' prior written notice to Provider. In such event, Company shall pay
Provider for accepted services properly performed through the effective
date
of termination and any approved, non-cancellable expenses incurred before
receipt of the termination notice.

Either party may terminate this Agreement immediately upon written notice if
the other party becomes insolvent, enters liquidation, makes an assignment
for the benefit of creditors, or becomes subject to a proceeding that is not
dismissed within the period permitted by applicable law.

Upon termination, each party shall return the other party's property and
confidential information as required by this Agreement. Termination shall
not affect rights or obligations that accrued before the effective
termination date.

8. AUTO-RENEWAL

This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and remain in effect for
an initial term of twelve (12) months.

After the initial term, this Agreement shall automatically renew for
successive twelve (12) month renewal periods unless either party provides
written notice of non-renewal at least sixty (60) days before the end of the
then-current term.

If either party provides timely notice of non-renewal, the Agreement shall
expire at the end of the applicable term and shall not automatically renew
for another period.

Any renewal period shall remain subject to the terms and conditions of this
Agreement unless the parties expressly agree otherwise in writing.

9. GOVERNING LAW

This Agreement and any dispute, claim, or controversy arising out of or
relating to this Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance
with the laws of the State of New York, without regard to its conflict of
laws principles.

The parties agree that the courts located in New York County, New York shall
have exclusive jurisdiction over any dispute arising out of or relating to
this Agreement, except where applicable law requires a different forum.

Each party irrevocably submits to the jurisdiction of such courts and waives
any objection based on inconvenient forum to the extent permitted by law.

10. DATA SECURITY

Provider shall maintain reasonable administrative, technical, and physical
safeguards designed to protect Company data against unauthorized access,
loss, destruction, alteration, or disclosure.

Provider shall restrict access to Company data to personnel who require such
access to perform their responsibilities under this Agreement. Provider
shall maintain appropriate access controls and shall review privileged
access periodically.

Provider shall notify Company promptly after becoming aware of a confirmed
security incident that materially affects Company data and shall reasonably
cooperate with Company in investigating and mitigating the incident.

11. AUDIT RIGHTS

Upon reasonable prior written notice and no more than once annually, Company
may audit Provider's compliance with the security and confidentiality
requirements of this Agreement.

Any audit shall be conducted during normal business hours and in a manner
designed to minimize unreasonable disruption to Provider's operations.

Provider shall reasonably cooperate with such audits and shall provide
relevant documentation reasonably necessary to demonstrate compliance,
subject to appropriate confidentiality protections.

12. INSURANCE

Provider shall maintain commercially reasonable insurance coverage
appropriate for the nature and scope of the services provided under this
Agreement.

Upon reasonable request, Provider shall provide certificates of insurance
confirming the existence of the required coverage.

13. FORCE MAJEURE

Neither party shall be responsible for delay or failure to perform an
obligation under this Agreement to the extent caused by events beyond its
reasonable control, including natural disasters, widespread
telecommunications failures, governmental actions, war, civil disturbance,
or other similar events.

The affected party shall promptly notify the other party of the event and
shall use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate its effects and resume
performance.

14. NOTICES

Any notice required under this Agreement shall be provided in writing by
email, recognized courier, or registered mail to the contact information
designated by the receiving party.

A notice shall be deemed received when delivery is confirmed by the relevant
communication method, subject to any mandatory requirements of applicable
law.

15. ASSIGNMENT

Neither party may assign this Agreement or transfer its rights or
obligations without the prior written consent of the other party, except
that either party may assign this Agreement to an affiliate or in connection
with a merger, reorganization, or sale of substantially all of its assets,
provided that the assignee assumes the assigning party's obligations.

16. ENTIRE AGREEMENT

This Agreement, together with all applicable Statements of Work and written
amendments signed by both parties, constitutes the entire agreement between
the parties concerning its subject matter and supersedes all prior
discussions, proposals, and agreements relating to that subject matter.

17. SEVERABILITY

If any provision of this Agreement is determined to be invalid or
unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall remain in full force and
effect, and the invalid or unenforceable provision shall be modified to the
minimum extent necessary to make it enforceable while preserving its
original intent as closely as possible.

18. NO WAIVER

A failure or delay by either party to exercise any right or remedy under
this Agreement shall not constitute a waiver of that right or remedy.
A waiver shall be effective only if made in writing by an authorized
representative of the waiving party.

19. COUNTERPARTS AND ELECTRONIC SIGNATURES

This Agreement may be executed in counterparts, each of which shall be
considered an original and all of which together shall constitute one
instrument.

Electronic signatures shall have the same legal effect as original
signatures to the extent permitted by applicable law.

20. GENERAL COMPLIANCE

Each party shall comply with all applicable laws and regulations relating to
its performance under this Agreement.

Each party shall maintain records reasonably necessary to demonstrate such
compliance and shall cooperate in good faith with reasonable requests from
the other party concerning compliance matters.

END OF AGREEMENT
